bindings.note: Same physical key as the JetBrains/VS Code Move Line Up/Down above — an existing 3-way alignment.
No VS Code equivalent command exists.
Strongest cross-app alignment in the project — matches Obsidian's own pre-existing binding. ctrl+y in VS Code deliberately displaces Redo (Redo stays on ctrl+shift+z).
Plain ctrl+j was rejected — it collides with JetBrains' own Live Template chord and VS Code's own Toggle Panel chord.
Plain ctrl+/ needs no VS Code entry — already the native default. ctrl+7 and numpad-divide are accommodations for a Spanish keyboard layout.

F2 is added alongside JetBrains' own inherited Shift+F6 default, not replacing it — both keys must be declared together or Shift+F6 would be lost. VS Code needs no entry, F2 is already its default. Also matches Nautilus's own F2=Rename convention.
Overlaps Nautilus's own ctrl+t = New Tab — accepted deliberately, matches the same convention browsers use.

bindings.action: Switch Tool Window (Project / Find / Run / Debug / Structure / VCS / ...)
bindings.note: Relocated off $default's own Alt+1..0 onto Ctrl+Alt+1..0 for consistency with the project's Ctrl-based convention. Plain Ctrl+0-9 and Ctrl+Shift+0-9 were already fully claimed in $default (GotoBookmarkN / ToggleBookmarkN), so Ctrl+Alt+digit is the free family — confirmed untouched by Omarchy/Hyprland (which only claims digit combos through Super: Super+N workspace switch, Super+Ctrl+N bar panels, Super+Alt+N group windows) and by VS Code (no default binding on Ctrl+Alt+digit). VS Code's own Ctrl+1-9 (focus editor group N) and Obsidian's own Mod+1-8 (go to tab N, its native default) are deliberately left alone — different concepts (editor groups, open tabs) from JetBrains tool windows, not something to force into false equivalence.

bindings.action: Select All Occurrences Under Cursor (multi-cursor edit)
bindings.note: VS Code needs no entry — ctrl+shift+l is already its native default (editor.action.selectHighlights) for this exact feature. JetBrains' own default was ctrl+alt+shift+j, moved here for cross-editor consistency. Obsidian has no equivalent command.

Requires the Markdown All in One VS Code extension (yzhang.markdown-all-in-one) — no built-in alternative exists. ctrl+shift+k displaces VS Code's own Delete Line default, which is harmless since Delete Line already lives on ctrl+y in this project. JetBrains keeps ctrl+shift+c alongside the new key rather than losing its native default. Obsidian's editor:toggle-code moved here from the ctrl+shift+= it had in every vault — there was never a technical reason for the split, only that the vaults already had their own key; ctrl+shift+k is free in Obsidian, whose only K default is Mod+K (Insert Link).

No JetBrains action exists for this at all (checked the full bundled Markdown plugin) — dropped there rather than building a custom Live Template, though ctrl+alt+k is confirmed free in $default if one is ever written. Requires the same Markdown All in One VS Code extension as surround-with-backticks. Obsidian's editor:insert-codeblock moved here from the ctrl+shift+\ it had in every vault, for the same reason as surround-with-backticks; ctrl+alt+k is free in Obsidian.

Moved from alt+p to ctrl+alt+p in all three (2026-09-23). VS Code has no single 'toggle pin' command (a feature request for one is still open upstream) — two conditional bindings simulate it. ctrl+alt+p is free in VS Code outside macOS (its only claim there is a Mac-only binding scoped to the Keyboard Shortcuts editor) and free in Obsidian, whose only P default is Mod+P (command palette). In JetBrains it is $default's IntroduceParameter (Extract Parameter): the empty-keys entry above renders as an <action> with no keyboard-shortcut children, which is how a child keymap drops an inherited shortcut, so Extract Parameter is deliberately left with no key at all.

Obsidian's own pre-existing key, extended to the other two. JetBrains' SelectInProjectView ('Select File in Project View') has no $default shortcut and ctrl+shift+y is free there. VS Code's showActiveFileInExplorer has no default shortcut either, but ctrl+shift+y is its Toggle Debug Console — removed here on purpose, the Debug Console is still a click away in the panel.

Moved off the vaults' old ctrl+shift+e / ctrl+shift+r, which are expensive in JetBrains ($default gives them to RecentLocations and ReplaceInPath), onto the ctrl+alt pair. ctrl+alt+r is already VS Code's own native key for revealFileInOS on Linux, so the entry mostly re-states it — and adds it on macOS, where VS Code's default is Cmd+Alt+R and a literal 'ctrl' means the Control key. JetBrains' OpenInAssociatedApplication ('Open in Associated Application') and RevealIn ('Show in File Manager') both exist with no $default shortcut; the only $default claims on these two chords are context-scoped (Console.History.Browse and ToggleFindInSelection on ctrl+alt+e, Diff.ApplyLeftSide on ctrl+alt+r) and are left alone. VS Code has no built-in 'open in the OS default app' command at all, so only the 'show' half reaches it.

ctrl+r is already JetBrains' $default for Replace, so JetBrains needs no entry — the unification is VS Code catching up with it and with Obsidian, which has used ctrl+r in every vault over its own Mod+H default. In VS Code ctrl+r is File > Open Recent; that default is removed so the chord means one thing everywhere. The when clause mirrors the precondition VS Code puts on its native ctrl+h.
Harmless no-op in a vault without the Tasks plugin installed.

ctrl+pageup / ctrl+pagedown is already the native key for exactly this action in both VS Code (previousEditor/nextEditor) and Obsidian (which binds ctrl+tab AND ctrl+pageup/pagedown by default), and it is the same convention browsers and Nautilus use — the cheapest possible unification. Declared for VS Code anyway because its macOS defaults are Cmd-based. JetBrains' PreviousTab/NextTab keep their inherited alt+left / alt+right as secondaries (declaring an action replaces its whole shortcut set), and there ctrl+pageup/pagedown only displaces the EditorMoveToPageTop/Bottom caret moves. Chosen over ctrl+tab precisely so JetBrains' Switcher and VS Code's MRU editor quick-pick both keep ctrl+tab; Obsidian's own ctrl+tab / ctrl+shift+tab defaults are listed here so that rewriting hotkeys.json does not silently drop them. All four Obsidian entries use the literal Ctrl modifier rather than Mod, matching Obsidian's own defaults: Mod would become Cmd on macOS, where Cmd+Tab is the OS app switcher and where JetBrains and VS Code both put this on the Control key.

bindings.action: Zoom In / Out (whole-app UI scale, not text size)
bindings.note: VS Code needs no entries — ctrl+plus/ctrl+minus are already its native zoom in/out on every platform. Nautilus already uses the same keys by its own convention. JetBrains' code-folding family (ExpandAll/CollapseAll and the Region variants) had claimed every two-modifier combination on plus/minus, so it's relocated to the three-modifier ctrl+alt+shift+plus/minus (preserving the original numpad-add/subtract secondaries) to free the two-modifier chord for zoom. Reset is deliberately NOT unified — each app keeps its own working default (JetBrains shift+alt+0, VS Code ctrl+numpad0, Obsidian ctrl+0) since forcing one key costs more than a rarely-used action is worth.

Adds ctrl+c/x/v as working shortcuts on macOS alongside the native Cmd+C/X/V, not replacing them (Obsidian entries use the literal Ctrl modifier rather than Mod for exactly this reason). JetBrains needs NO entry at all — $Copy/$Cut/$Paste already inherit control C/X/V from $default with classic secondaries (control INSERT, shift DELETE, shift INSERT); declaring an override here would replace and lose those secondaries for no benefit. VS Code's own ctrl+c/x/v for these commands are gated to non-Mac platforms by VS Code itself, so this only adds real capability on Mac (harmless no-op on Linux, which already has it natively). OPEN QUESTION carried over: Cmd+C/V may not actually work in the JetBrains editor at all under this project's $default-based keymap (a pre-existing characteristic unrelated to this binding) — unverified without a Mac, worth checking for real.
